name: xAI

profile.reading: This is the original building of xAI's Colossus supercomputer campus in South Memphis, at 3231 Riverport Road. The site is a former Electrolux appliance factory (785,000 square feet), purchased by Phoenix Investors in December 2023 for $35 million; its existing shell and proximity to wastewater treatment infrastructure and the Mississippi River let xAI complete construction in roughly 122 days, versus an industry-standard multi-year timeline, with Dell Technologies and Supermicro handling infrastructure and Nvidia supplying GPU hardware. xAI, incorporated by Elon Musk in March 2023, finalized its decision to build in Memphis in March 2024, announced the project publicly in June 2024, began operations in July 2024, and officially launched Colossus with 100,000 GPUs in September 2024, primarily to train xAI's Grok chatbot while also supporting X (formerly Twitter) and SpaceX workloads. By June 2025 the GPU count had grown to roughly 150,000 H100, 50,000 H200, and 30,000 GB200 units, with power consumption rising from about 150 MW at launch to a 250 MW maximum, an amount well beyond the facility's original 150 MW grid connection, so xAI has supplemented it with 35 gas turbines (422 MW combined capacity) and 168 Tesla Megapack batteries. That gas-turbine buildout drew significant environmental scrutiny: the Southern Environmental Law Center has characterized the facility as likely the largest industrial emitter of nitrogen oxides in Memphis, citing an estimated 1,200 to 2,000 tons of NOx annually, and xAI initially operated the turbines without permits under a Shelby County regulatory loophole covering only generators on-site 365-plus days, before EPA standards revised in January 2026 required permits for large temporary methane turbines. Water usage (an expected 5 million-plus gallons daily) and local arsenic-contamination concerns prompted an approved $80 million wastewater recycling facility. No formal public review process preceded the project's announcement, and Memphis residents have reported chronic respiratory issues and learned of the facility primarily from local news coverage rather than a community process.

reading:
xAI is Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company, founded in 2023, privately held and not an SEC filer, with offices in Palo Alto, California reported by real estate trade press in January 2026. Following its 2025 merger with X, formerly Twitter, the copyright notice on its own site reads SpaceXAI LLC, reflecting a tighter corporate tie to Musk's other companies. It is in this registry as a hyperscaler, and its three Tennessee rows all sit in Memphis, where the company built the fastest large compute ramp any operator in this dataset has publicly documented.

The flagship is Colossus, built into a former Electrolux manufacturing plant in South Memphis. The build decision was taken in March 2024, announced in June 2024, and the first phase went live in September 2024 with 100,000 Nvidia H100 GPUs installed in 122 days. By December 2024 the installation had doubled to 200,000 GPUs and peak power draw rose from 150 to 250 megawatts. By June 2025 the configuration was reported as roughly 150,000 H100, 50,000 H200 and 30,000 GB200 accelerators, with a further 110,000 GB200 units planned for a second site, against a stated ambition of reaching a million GPUs. Grid supply came to about 150 megawatts over an existing line, with a second substation adding roughly another 150 megawatts, and xAI requested on the order of 1.1 gigawatts for its expansion.

The reason this operator has an unusually thick public record is what xAI did about the gap between what the grid could deliver and what the buildout needed. It installed gas turbines on the Memphis site and ran them. That is on site generation, and it should not be confused with either critical IT load or the diesel standby plant that most data centres keep. The turbines produce the power, they do not measure the computing. Residents, the Southern Environmental Law Center and local groups argued the turbines had been operating for more than a year without the permits the Clean Air Act requires before construction of a major source. The Shelby County Health Department issued a minor source air permit for fifteen turbines on 2 July 2025, over more than two thousand opposing comments, having treated others as nonroad engines exempt from permitting. The NAACP Memphis branch and Young, Gifted and Green appealed to the Memphis and Shelby County Air Pollution Control Board on 16 July 2025, arguing that up to 35 turbines had run unpermitted and that the site qualified as an existing major source requiring prevention of significant deterioration review. On 16 December 2025 the board dismissed the appeal on mootness grounds rather than on the merits.

The dispute then moved to federal court. In 2026 the NAACP, represented by the Southern Environmental Law Center and Earthjustice, brought a Clean Air Act citizen suit against xAI and its subsidiary MZX Tech over the power plant serving Colossus 2, and filed a motion for a preliminary injunction on 6 May 2026, which was pending as this entry was written. The plaintiffs say that after a notice of violation in February 2026 xAI added six further turbines, bringing that plant to 33 units. That second plant sits in Southaven, Mississippi, outside the Tennessee rows this registry holds for xAI, but it is the same buildout and the same regulatory question.
